> Thinking about it, the same applies to `Range` requests or progress upload events

I guess the `Range` requests part is debatable though, as one could want their Service Worker to cache videos for offline use; in practical purpose though, it's still not a great developer experience that these are broken by default IMO. Corresponding GH issue is in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/25865.

Thx for the detailed write-up and the reproduction, @laurentgoudet :+1:

Yeah, `Range` requests are different (and _could_ be handled by the SW). Let's keep tracking that in #25865.

Regarding `POST` requests, there _is_ value in them going through the SW (even if just to pass through to the network in the end). For example `DataGroup` uses them to [invalidate caches][1].

I do agree, though, that it doesn't make much sense for the SW to return `index.html` (aka the app shell) for non-GET requests. I.e. we could add an extra check for `req.method === 'GET'` [here][2].

##
Would you, by any chance, be interested in submitting a pull request, @laurentgoudet?

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ec8bae1b2772b68416e1469ff680caaf433aac28/packages/service-worker/worker/src/data.ts#L319-L332
[2]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ec8bae1b2772b68416e1469ff680caaf433aac28/packages/service-worker/worker/src/app-version.ts#L180
I try to understand this issue. Can anyone tell me where I am wrong? I've cloned the author's repo and started the app. The displayed form was sent with no redirects to `index.html`.

> Regarding `POST` requests, there _is_ value in them going through the SW (even if just to pass through to the network in the end). For example `DataGroup` uses them to [invalidate caches](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ec8bae1b2772b68416e1469ff680caaf433aac28/packages/service-worker/worker/src/data.ts#L319-L332).

Right yeah I had seen that code, and I do agree that it can make sense to flush a cache entry after a mutation, although it mostly applies to data requests (we serialize the Redux store state into local storage and don't use the SW worker for that).

However, I'd still argue that - until Service Workers get better - all the "potentially broken" features should be opt-in rather than opt-out. In short, that would mean an opposite mechanism to `ngsw-bypass`, which would require oneself to explicitly opt-in to certain features, e.g.:
- Pass a `ngsw-enable-mutations` header to opt-in to `POST`/`PUT` requests being handed, i.e. allowing cache invalidation (but breaking upload progress events)
- Pass a `ngsw-enable-range` query param to opt-in to `Range` requests being handled, i.e. allowing media files to be accessed offline (but breaking seeking)
- Probably something similar for HTTP Basic Auth, as I just realized that it was broken as well.

My point is that it's much easier to add these extra request headers / query params incrementally in a brand new app (with HTTP interceptors & the like), when ones needs to, compared to the current state of the Angular Service Worker (by default) breaking a lot of different features web sites have relived on for a long time.

It would provide a better & safer developer experience, while still allowing advanced use cases when needed, the longer term goal being to scrap them when `Fetch` is where it needs to be basically.

> I do agree, though, that it doesn't make much sense for the SW to return `index.html` (aka the app shell) for non-GET requests. I.e. we could add an extra check for `req.method === 'GET'` [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ec8bae1b2772b68416e1469ff680caaf433aac28/packages/service-worker/worker/src/app-version.ts#L180).

> Would you, by any chance, be interested in submitting a pull request, @laurentgoudet?

Yep I'll try to look into that next week as it's a different issue to the broader discussion.

> I try to understand this issue. Can anyone tell me where I am wrong? I've cloned the author's repo and started the app. The displayed form was sent with no redirects to `index.html`.

Check that the SW has been properly activated, e.g. Service Workers are disabled in Firefox Private browsing for instance.

> Check that the SW has been properly activated, e.g. Service Workers are disabled in Firefox Private browsing for instance.

This error does not occur in Chrome or Firefox. In the `Application -> Service Workers` tab I can see that the provided SW has been activated and my `index.html` is served by it.
